name: Humanities Helping Hands: the library of proven facts

labels.PROVEN: a machine checked the statement in checked_as
labels.ARITHMETIC-CHECKED: a machine checked only the arithmetic in checked_as; the real-world claim is OPEN
labels.GUESS: claim_label: a person matched the English words to the proven statement
labels.OPEN: claim_label: a real-world fact; only the numbers in it are proven

facts.claim: Daniel's Root Theorem: fixing a mistake once, at the root, never costs more than fixing its copies in every layer above it, and costs strictly less once it has spread to two or more layers
facts.label: PROVEN
facts.checked_as: c ≤ n × c, and c < n × c when n ≥ 2 and c > 0

facts.claim: Daniel's Founder's Claim: if, every week, the library of proven facts grows at least as much as the cost of finding a new one, its lead never shrinks; if it grows strictly more, the lead grows every week
facts.label: PROVEN
facts.checked_as: facts − cost never falls when Δfacts ≥ Δcost each week, and strictly rises when Δfacts > Δcost
facts.not_proven: Lean proves the "if, then". Whether the library really grows faster than its cost is measured week by week, and the first verdict is due 2026-11-08.

facts.claim: P vs NP, the easy half: checking a proposed answer to any SAT puzzle (Boolean rules over switches) is fast and right, so SAT is in NP
facts.label: PROVEN
facts.checked_as: the checker says yes exactly when every rule is met, in at most one step per switch mention and per rule, plus one
facts.not_proven: This is the known, easy half: checking. Whether finding an answer can always be as fast as checking one is P vs NP itself, and it stays OPEN.

facts.claim: Circuits of bounded depth built from AND, OR, NOT and counting-mod-p gates need a huge number of gates to count mod a different prime q
facts.label: PROVEN
facts.checked_as: for primes p ≠ q, any such circuit of depth d computing MOD_q on n inputs has size at least exponential in a power of n (the bound is written out in full)
facts.not_proven: This is a machine-checked formalization of the known 1987 Razborov-Smolensky theorem: not new math, and not P vs NP.

facts.claim: The algebrization barrier: there is an oracle, with a low-degree extension over every finite field, relative to which NP is not in P
facts.label: PROVEN
facts.checked_as: Aaronson and Wigderson Theorem 5.3: an oracle A and its degree-2 extensions over every GF(x) with NP^A not contained in P^Ã
facts.not_proven: This is a machine-checked formalization of the known 2009 Aaronson-Wigderson algebrization barrier: not new math, and not P vs NP.

facts.claim: Formula lower bounds: Subbotovskaya's shrinkage, Khrapchenko's bound for parity, and Andreev's function needing large formulas
facts.label: PROVEN
facts.checked_as: Khrapchenko: edges(A,B)² ≤ size × |A| × |B|; Andreev: (2^r − 2)/(4r) − 1 ≤ (r/2^r)^(3/2) × formula size
facts.not_proven: This is a machine-checked formalization of the known results Subbotovskaya 1961, Khrapchenko 1971, Andreev 1987: not new math, and not P vs NP. Andreev's bound says something only from r = 5 up, and the decomposition lemma counts pieces only.
